resources.string: Shows a Vakya bubble in WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram and Messages. When you tap it, Vakya reads the messages on screen and suggests replies in your style, then types the one you pick into the message box. It never sends anything for you.

Vakya uses Android's Accessibility service to:

• Read the messages visible in the chat you're in when you tap the Vakya bubble, only in the chat apps you tick in Vakya (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Messages; WhatsApp until you choose). Android sends Vakya nothing from any other app.
• Type the reply you pick into the message box. It never presses Send.
• If "Learn from messages I send" is on, save the messages you send in those apps, and what they were replying to, on this phone only. This teaches Vakya your style and builds your reply bank: your own past replies, suggested instantly without AI.

To make suggestions, the visible messages (plus a small cropped copy of the newest photo or sticker they sent, if "Look at photos and stickers" is on), your style card, a few of your past messages to that contact and your notes about them are sent to your Vakya server, which passes them to an AI service: Groq, or Google Gemini for Kannada-English chats and whenever Groq is busy. The Vakya server doesn't store them. Gemini is used on Google's free tier, where Google may use what it receives to improve its products and people at Google may review it. With your own Groq key, nothing goes to Google. Each AI service's own privacy terms apply. Nobody at Vakya reads your chats: the server never saves or logs them, and its code is public at github.com/skandaumesh/vakya.
